notes.title: Old version available for players with issues
notes.content: [h2]Maintenance Patch[/h2][p]Our latest maintenance patch was a well over-due patch that upgraded our outdated code, engine, plug-ins, internal systems and more, which is necessary as preparation for the crossplay update that will be released with the Switch releases later this year. [/p][p]With this, we've seen that the requirements to smoothly run the game have also shifted and lower-end systems that were able to run the game before, could now experience more issues with the game. Since our older games did not save player save files in the cloud, but instead saved these locally, this migration did not go smoothly for everyone. We've seen that our code was not able to detect the save files successfully for everyone, resulting into some players losing their saves. [/p][p][/p][h2]Re-selecting your checkpoint:[/h2][p]Most players will have to [b]re-select their checkpoint[/b] file by clicking on "change" in the menu, followed by "start new journey" to then select your checkpoint.[/p][p]For players who are unable to select their checkpoint or are unable to smoothly play the game due to performance or connection issues, we have added an [b]old version of the game[/b] before the patch.[/p][p][/p][h2]To select the legacy version:[/h2][olist][*][p]Right click [i]We Were Here Together[/i] in your Steam library[/p][/*][*][p]Go to [i]Properties[/i][/p][/*][*][p]Click on [i]Betas[/i][/p][/*][*][p]In the drop down menu, select [i]Legacy - PATCH #1.7.6[/i][/p][/*][/olist][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: The We Were Here series is coming to Nintendo Switch!
notes.content:
[h2]Dear Explorers,[/h2][p][/p][p]Some of you know these halls all too well. You’ve wandered the frozen corridors of Castle Rock, walkie-talkie in hand, voice cracking through the static. You’ve solved puzzles, shouted directions, cracked codes, and yes, maybe left your partner behind once or twice. It happens.[/p][p]For years, the [i]We Were Here[/i] series has tested friendships on PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. Now, it’s time for a new expedition.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]We’re super excited to announce that [i]We Were Here[/i], [i]We Were Here Too[/i], and [i]We Were Here Together[/i] are coming to Nintendo Switch![/b][/h3][p][/p][previewyoutube="TF6n0lMsYv0;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Your favourite co-op adventure is going handheld (or docked, if you want to see your friend betray you on the big screen).[/p][p]To play on Switch, you’ll need two things: a Nintendo Switch Online Membership and an external microphone. The trilogy will also be backwards compatible with the Switch 2, so whether you’re playing on shiny new hardware or your trusty old console, you can still team up together. As always, you and your friend will both need a separate copy of the game you want to play.

If you're new here, [i]We Were Here[/i] games are all about two players, trapped apart in a forgotten place, trying to escape through communication alone. You won’t see each other, and can only talk to each other over your walkie-talkies. Every puzzle you solve depends on how well you work together.[/p][p]If you’re a weathered Explorer, this is your chance to bring a new partner to Castle Rock. That friend who only games on Switch? Time to hand them a walkie-talkie and hope they’re better at reading runes than you were.[/p][p][/p][p]Whether you're playing curled up in a blanket fort or squeezed into a train seat, remember:[/p][p]You’re never truly alone…[/p][p][/p][h3]See you on the other end of the walkie-talkie,
[b]Total Mayhem Games[/b][/h3]

notes.title: Our Great Studio Migration!
notes.content:
[i]2024 was a year in which our mighty developers haven’t been sitting still—quite the opposite. After months of exploring all the crooks and crannies of the vast terrain of Rotterdam, we have secured a beautiful and spacious new base in the booming city center![/i]

[h2]We are growing![/h2]

Over the past year, our numbers have swelled, welcoming a host of talented and inspiring individuals to the fold. This is great news, but it did come with a downside. Our once-spacious studio at Schiehavenkade began to feel... rather snug. Long queues for the microwaves during feeding hours, overheated meeting rooms, and desks encroaching dangerously close to the entrance—a sure sign it was time to seek new territory. The best part: we have [url=https://youtu.be/oC5Hpgu9VVI]documented[/url] the entire move!

[previewyoutube=oC5Hpgu9VVI;full][/previewyoutube]

We hold beautiful memories of the games we created in our old studio and can’t wait to see what magic unfolds in our new home.

Curious to see where all the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/sale/WWHfranchise]We Were Here games[/url] were made? Find them all in this map, including our dev's favourite hotspots!

notes.title: Happy frenniversary! 🎉
notes.content:
[h1]Dear Explorers,[/h1]

[h2]Happy Frenniversary! 🎉[/h2]

It’s been one whole year since we launched We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip, and what an incredible year it’s been! Let’s take a trip down memory lane and revisit the exciting moments from the reveal of this special game.

[h2]Crafting a Secret[/h2]

After the release of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1341290/We_Were_Here_Forever/]We Were Here Forever[/url] in 2022, our team started plotting the next chapter in the We Were Here series. With Forever being our longest and most intricate adventure, packed with puzzles, mysteries, and expansive locations, we knew we wanted to offer something a little different next. This time, we aimed for something short, sweet, and perfect for explorers who want a bite-sized co-op experience.

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2296990/We_Were_Here_Expeditions_The_FriendShip/]We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip[/url] was born—a game designed to be fun, challenging, and most of all, an absolute blast to play with your friends, whether they’re seasoned fans of the We Were Here series or joining us for the first time.

[h2]The Big Reveal at WASD x IGN 🎮[/h2]

Now, we couldn’t just launch The FriendShip like any ordinary game. No, we wanted to do something BIG—something that would surprise and delight our amazing community! So, we decided to go full stealth mode, keeping the entire game a secret until its grand reveal at WASD x IGN. And what’s better than a surprise? A free surprise! 🎁 We dropped the game for free for the first month, allowing millions of you to hop aboard and set sail on this new co-op adventure.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44619513/2b7241314815735337511a526af068ba87da39bd.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44619513/2b7241314815735337511a526af068ba87da39bd.jpg[/img][/url]

The response was overwhelming! Over 6 million explorers claimed The FriendShip, joining our ever-growing We Were Here family. 💖

[h2]Celebrating Friendship 🫶[/h2]

At Total Mayhem Games, friendship is the heart and soul of everything we create. It’s the thread that ties all our games together, and it’s the bond we share with you, our amazing explorers. We simply couldn’t have reached this point without your endless love and support.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44619513/e0b56b7e1c49f6f6b1cd9835a6031e31c31463c1.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44619513/e0b56b7e1c49f6f6b1cd9835a6031e31c31463c1.png[/img][/url]

And guess what? There’s more on the horizon! We've got some exciting stuff coming up. So stay tuned, and always remember: “There are good ships, and wood ships, ships that sail the sea. But the best ships are friendships, and may they always be!”

Here’s to many more adventures together!

[h3]All the best,
Total Mayhem Games[/h3]

notes.title: Say hello to our new game: We Were Here Forever!
notes.content:
[h2][i][b]...does one ever truly escape Castle Rock?[/b][/i][/h2]
Find out in our new game [i]We Were Here Forever![/i] Prepare for Castle Rock to be more lively than ever before, with puzzles that are even more engaging, more dynamic, and will challenge you in multiple ways. 

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33592243/6e7494d00c7144acaf5bb76142574080e682e7dc.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33592243/6e7494d00c7144acaf5bb76142574080e682e7dc.jpg[/img][/url]

[i]We Were Here Forever[/i] will tell you a tale of the past and the future of Castle Rock, like you’ve never experienced before. The stage is set - you and a friend are trapped in the realm of Castle Rock with no way out - were you betrayed, or simply not that clever? Be aware, nothing is what it seems - there is a mystery buried deep in the heart of the Keep. Locked up with just a pair of walkie-talkies and your wits, will you be able to escape the Castle… forever?! Our announcement trailer will give you a taste of what's to come...

[previewyoutube=34R0UCd493M;full][/previewyoutube]
If that sounds good, you can wishlist the game on Steam right now!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1341290/We_Were_Here_Forever/

[h2]There's much more to learn![/h2]
Did you know... the torch in those screenshots isn't just for show? Helpful items may be key to your escape. Another new features in [i]Forever[/i] is how the story progresses - we wanted players to have a little more agency, so the storyline is now partially non-linear. You have some power to decide the order of events and how you explore the realm of Castle Rock.

This is just the tip of the iceberg though! We have much more to reveal as release day draws closer. If you want to make sure you don’t miss any updates on the game’s release, be sure you follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/WeWereHereGame]Twitter[/url] and join the lore discussions with fellow explorers on our [url=https://discord.gg/Pr72dKUFdK]Discord[/url]!

[h2]Other exciting WWH news![/h2]
We'll close out this post with a sale and the arrival of Castle Rock in new territory... we recently launched the [i]We Were Here[/i] games on PlayStation! Nowhere can escape the reach of Castle Rock ;)

If you haven't experienced the complete story of the We Were Here Series, now's your chance! Both [i][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/677160/We_Were_Here_Too/]We Were Here Too[/url][/i] and [i][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/865360/We_Were_Here_Together/]We Were Here Together[/url][/i] are on sale to celebrate the announcement of [i]We Were Here Forever![/i] The first game, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/582500/We_Were_Here/]We Were Here,[/url] remains free on Steam as always! Just the thing to tempt your friends inside Castle Rock - and once they're inside, well...

[i]Yours Forever,[/i]
[b]Total Mayhem Games [/b]

[h3]A year of Total Mayhem[/h3]
This past year was quite an adventure for us at the studio, full of intriguing puzzles and great highlights! One of the most memorable moments for us was the release of [i]We Were Here Together[/i] - it was humbling to see our game in the top steam sellers for October 2019. To date we've almost sold 100,000 copies of [i]We Were Here Together[/i]. Thank you all for your support!

To get a peek at how the year was for us developers, take a look at our series of Developer Diaries series: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8tThcTabRnU&list=PLHCVEMHWZo4TZVWjKAiVw0VcvQkOm_-Po
Three episodes are live already, and the fourth and final installment will be live on December 30th!

Another cherished moment was the release of [i]We Were Here[/i] and [i]We Were Here Too[/i] on Xbox One. The inclusion of [i]We Were Here[/i] in the ‘Games for Gold’ helped introduce a lot of new players to the series. We can’t wait to release [i]We Were Here Together[/i] on Xbox One as well in 2020!

We’ve also been nominated as one of the top 100 games in the Adventure category on IndieDB. With less than two days of voting left, [url=https://t.co/euM54U0sLT?amp=1]your support would be greatly appreciated![/url]

We also would like to take the time to thank the community for another awesome year, our partners for their great support and we want to wish you all happy Holidays and hopefully a new year with even more awesomeness for you all.

[h3]Christmas Changelog[/h3]
[b]New Features:[/b]
[list][*] Added a christmas themed puzzle to the basecamp.
[*] Revamp of the default controls. Player who have played before will keep their settings.
[*] Skipping a cutscene is now done by a HOLD action.[/list]
[b]Resolved Voice Issues:[/b]
[list][*] The incoming voice volume is no longer bound to master volume. This should fix some volume issues with the voice chat.
[*] Added experimental audio settings - marked in yellow - to test out. We would love to hear any feedback regarding the functionality of these settings. (The ‘Microphone level’ slider is set to your system level by default. Adjustments are directly applied to your system microphone level)[/list]
[b]Resolved Issues:[/b]
[list][*] Intro animation Wall is now synced properly.
[*] Mirror Room paintings should no longer fully rotate when clicked once.
[*] Players should no longer be able to jump in or out of a rotating door in the cave while it is rotating to prevent softlocking.
[*] Added proper controller button images to the menu.
[*] Fixed several desync issues in the mirror room.
[*] The purple orb pistons should now be retract on both sides in the mirror room.
[*] Optimized a ton of meshes throughout the game increasing performance.
[*] Selected button behaviour in the menus should now be more intuitive and consistent.
[*] Fixed several audio effects.
[*] Fixed some edge cases around inviting and leaving a session just before starting.
[*] Gamepad horizontal/vertical look speed should feel more consistent now.
[*] Changed some visual UI elements throughout the game.
[*] Fixed several seams in meshes throughout the game.
[*] Fixed an issue where spamming the ‘switch side’ button in the lobby would cause a desync.

notes.title: Dev Diary - Composing the We Were Here Together Theme
notes.content:
Hi everyone!
My name is Leon van der Stel and I'll be talking today about the creation of the main theme for [i]We Were Here Together[/i]. 
The first and second [i]We Were Here[/i] games share the same main theme. For the third entry in the series, we wanted a new main theme - the classic [i]We Were Here[/i] atmosphere in a new jacket. I would like to take you into the story behind the main theme and the choices that were made along the way. At different sections I'll link to audio clips. These are interim versions and ideas for the main theme that show the development process well. 

For the people who want to play the main theme themselves, I made sheet music, which you can find at the end of this dev diary. Finally, I want to thank Jos Platschorre for helping to compose the main theme with his grandiose guitar playing, and Tom Hartman for his support and feedback.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33592243/df8a7ca879b5944a0cab486df4730555fd7c633d.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33592243/df8a7ca879b5944a0cab486df4730555fd7c633d.png[/img][/url]
[i]The author, making music.[/i]

[h1]The process[/h1]
The most important thing with each piece of music is which feeling it must express. Since We Were Here Together is about two explorers alone in Antarctica, the terms [i]cold, deserted and isolated [/i]occurred to me. Although these were good terms, there was still something missing in my opinion. In the story, the other two explorers become hopeful when their emergency signal is fired into the air. Therefore the word [i]hope [/i]should also be included in the overall picture.

Now that the atmosphere has been determined, how do you implement this, and with which instruments? This is a question that you can only answer by getting started and carefully directing the result at every step. Having said that, I thought it would be cool to take the first steps with some guitar. 

This idea was inspired by the OST of [i]The Last of Us[/i], and it was in line with the direction which the TMG team and I wanted to go. My goal was to raise the standard to produce a greater result and I felt that this could only be achieved by involving other musicians. Fortunately I knew a good guitarist, Jos Platschorre, whose playing style would fit well with what I had in mind. After a phone call he agreed to help me to make something beautiful.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DvNF51-TSAQ&list=RDDvNF51-TSAQ&start_radio=1&t=0
Below are some of the first jams with Jos that had the most impact on the end result:

Jam 1A: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1hBcBzJ6AHzFiIa8lKR-POas_0cztGHF1
Jam 1B: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1vXODQNocPnziMArbSZu-jo5S2QHL4jbn
Jam 2: https://drive.google.com/open?id=19M0KITCgaRhj0bCu0_wk_Rgs2VbA8F5n

When listening to the above jams, several parts immediately jumped out that fit well with the new main theme vibe. Keeping in mind the [i]cold [/i]and [i]isolated [/i]atmosphere, the start of jam 2 was very satisfying. This stayed into place since then. After jam 1A was recorded, I had the impression that a strum style could fit in boldly with this (jam 1B). Although the Total Mayhem Games team was delighted with the vibe of these early jams, a simple and recognizable melody was still missing. Based on these jams, I came up with the following melody, to be played on the piano. The chord changes, the guitar style and the melody were the starting point for the next step.

Jam 3 - Piano melody: https://drive.google.com/open?id=13WdJvoi7V5Gr9ewBu8Dq953SpYKe6sGF

The following fragment contains the points above combined with the melody partially incorporated. In the second part I experimented with midi controller pads and vocals.

Jam 4: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1FvuxmTSr_Bda9ys4DZJZ0VotSRsYS3aq

At this point it was starting to become more viable and I was pleased with how the melody was incorporated with the guitar scrum. However, it still didn’t jive just yet; it sounded more like a loop. I was fortunate at this point to get some good advice from talented musician Tom Hartman on how it could potentially be turned into a good swinging melody that tells a story. Below is a take that he sent during a meeting. This recording inspired me during the composition of the end result.

Jam 5: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1T3fy3hIFwqJBtkhlFWiVVMymqaCbXcnk

So with this new jam in mind, I went back to the drawing board. The following jam (which is divided into two audio clips) was created by editing the old jams to be closer to the feel of Tom's recorded take (jam 5). Based on these new ideas, I selected a high pitched piano to incorporate into the theme - this piano with a lot of echo gave a [i]hopeful [/i]feeling, which you’ll recall is one of the expressions I added to my list at the beginning.

Jam 6: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1x4jtyLCMuY-arcSdi3HBxjAuhojQOFKs
Jam 7: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1eJB9MhZTF1i-l95vfVN5GVHVV75YcLWM

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33592243/dcfe259a9ac616d52c38ee7979c3ce121df8eb69.png[/img]
[i]This is NOT what the composition process looked like, for the record.[/i]

[h1]Fitting the pieces together[/h1]
As you can see, every decision at each step has had a part in shaping the music into what it is today. Although many ideas were collected, a complete composition was still missing. Even though the individual parts sounded good,  the overall composition is what makes or breaks it as a piece of music. From this point on, I didn't want to create new content anymore, but instead wanted to use what I had.

During this stage, the guitarist and I tried various parts on the spot in different combinations and listened for what felt best. Afterwards the composition was recorded in six takes. The last addition that has been made to the main theme was done by not ending with the [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonic_(music)]tonic[/url]. This gives a dissonant / out-of-place feeling that is also in line with some of our aforementioned expressions: [i]cold, deserted and isolated[/i].

[b]And so, the final composition was:[/b]

[b]Intro:[/b] 		Beginning of Jam 3
[b]Section A: [/b]	Main tune (Jam 6 + Jam 7)
[b]Section B:[/b]	Start Jam 2 with the main guitar style of the main tune
[b]Section C: [/b]	Section A, but layered with high pitched piano and pads

https://youtu.be/61kT23qnRGo

In summary, it has been a long journey. My secret ingredient is taking little steps, building upon things that feel right along the way, and to simply ask for help when necessary to get to the next stage. This is not just for music! The same strategy could be applied to all things and decisions in life.

If you are interested in playing the theme yourself, don't forget to check the main theme sheet music below. If you prefer just listening, you should visit our new [url=https://open.spotify.com/album/07BbfF6rf2TQ2i2IpXY719?si=axWOWvQ-Rp6TGyRATf-fsA]Spotify channel[/url]! Peace out :D

[b]Main Theme sheet music links[/b]
Interactive online: [url=https://flat.io/score/5d73748133d5ed32e1fc61d1-we-were-here-together-main-theme?sharingKey=93101f350e5331c1530d8eaae0cef7960c0cc9249bb4d065446c8be2936d13a04b2af7e6347f9a94aceeccadafc70dbffe8b0a7f7a6f1025898b49db068fd90e]https://flat.io/score/5d73748133d5ed32e1fc61d1-we-were-here-together-main-theme?sharingKey=93101f350e5331c1530d8eaae0cef7960c0cc9249bb4d065446c8be2936d13a04b2af7e6347f9a94aceeccadafc70dbffe8b0a7f7a6f1025898b49db068fd90e[/url]
PDF: [url=https://drive.google.com/open?id=1blfLqwVgHn9YvQVsVNtza-6dfB1jv7ia]https://drive.google.com/open?id=1blfLqwVgHn9YvQVsVNtza-6dfB1jv7ia[/url]

Cheers Leon

notes.title: We Were Here Together - Out Now
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=XhE5mPCHdY4;full][/previewyoutube]
[h1]Return to Castle Rock![/h1]
[i]We’re so excited![/i] The game is ready for you to play! For the first time, chill out in the Basecamp and set foot in the Antarctic snow on your way to Castle Rock.

You can get [i]We Were Here Together[/i] right now on Steam for $12.99 / €12.99. There is a launch discount of 5%, and players of earlier We Were Here games will get [b]an extra 10% discount![/b]

The third game in the [i]We Were Here[/i] series features new gameplay mechanics, locations, an inventory for you to fill with curious items, and of course new puzzles. In response to your requests, there is more emphasis on story than ever before, and several large environments to explore and solve puzzles within.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33592243/c3ea4f6faa8cb94657c38b8ad5ff709cf69c1024.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33592243/c3ea4f6faa8cb94657c38b8ad5ff709cf69c1024.png[/img][/url]
[i]Your adventure will start out at the base camp...[/i]

There are several great innovations in [i]We Were Here Together[/i], and it's hard for us to pick a favourite! One thing we do know is that there are some amazing new environments for you to explore on your journey from the expedition base camp to the inhospitable Antarctic mystery that is Castle Rock. Read on and we'll tell you more about those and other features in our latest and greatest adventure yet! 

[b]Features include:[/b]
[list][*]Even closer coop – you won’t always be split up from your partner this time. Explore together, try both sides of a puzzle for a different perspective, it’s up to you! Just don’t get too comfortable - Castle Rock has some tricks waiting for you…
[*]The great outdoors – puzzle outside Castle Rock for the first time, from the deceptively cosy expedition base camp through imposing sub-zero valleys to breath-taking frozen caves.
[*]Gadgets won’t save you - but they might help! Figure out how to use new equipment and gather an inventory of curious items to solve puzzles and progress towards the fateful finale in [i]We Were Here Together[/i].
[*]You aren’t alone in Castle Rock – and this time you get to meet a fellow explorer who is trapped inside. Could they know a way out… and can you trust them?[/list] 
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33592243/c45e7bb15ccd5d661462a012e98b780924805539.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33592243/c45e7bb15ccd5d661462a012e98b780924805539.png[/img][/url]
[i]You will travel through the icy wastes...[/i]

More than 2,000,000 people have played [i]We Were Here[/i] and [i]We Were Here Too[/i] since their releases. It's amazing to see how much you all love what we've made, and we couldn't have done it without the support from all of you! We'd like to give a special thanks to the alpha and beta testers with their great feedback - you'll be getting special walkie-talkie skins as our way of showing our gratitude, along with a place in the credits! 

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33592243/67daf72bbd9e49217cf26b969f50695c40c28ede.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33592243/67daf72bbd9e49217cf26b969f50695c40c28ede.png[/img][/url]
[i]...and who knows where you'll end up?[/i]

[h1]But wait, there’s more![/h1] 
The [i]We Were Here Together[/i] Supporter Edition contains a special walkie-talkie skin, beautiful artworks designed especially for desktop or phone backgrounds, and almost an hour of music.

For newcomers and those who haven’t got the complete collection yet, check out the We Were Here Series Bundle! It does what it says on the can, with all three games, two supporter editions, and every soundtrack in one tidy collection.

[h1]We hope you enjoy your Antarctic adventure! Maybe you'll even make it back alive? We’d love to hear all about your adventure, so let us know![/h1]

notes.title: On the lookout for new puzzle testers!
notes.content:
[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33592243/89c173ef8ef232a6f574ccf0eaba089300cf4062.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33592243/89c173ef8ef232a6f574ccf0eaba089300cf4062.png[/img][/url]
Hello Antarctic explorers! We are looking for more people to give feedback on our early versions of the new puzzles. The testing will be done between April 5th and May 3rd. If you think that you and a friend might be up for it, read on!

[h1]How will it work?[/h1]
We will release a new puzzle every Friday. The first puzzle will be released on the 5th of April at 19:00. The last puzzle will be released on the 3rd of May. Puzzles are fully playable for two people, but not yet polished to the high standard you can expect from us in the final release. When you are selected, we will assign you a single puzzle / area to play in a particular week, based on when you’re available. More time may be granted for testing if we decide a puzzle could benefit from additional testing and feedback.

On top of having the opportunity to see new puzzles develop, testers will get credited in the game with their Steam profile name.The first 100 applicants who fit our requirements will be accepted into the testing program. If you aren’t one of the first 100, don't feel disappointed yet as we might still ask you to join testing in the future if it turns out that we need additional testers.

[h1]How can I join?[/h1]
There has been a lot of interest in testing the game, and therefore we're closing applications for now. Thanks to everyone who has mailed us and you will all receive an answer, but it might take a bit longer than expected due to the volume of requests. Thanks for your patience!


Include the following:
[*]Your Steam profile name.
[*]Your partner’s Steam profile name.
[*]A short explanation of why you two want to join the testing and why you think you could be helpful.
[*]Which weeks (running from Friday to Thursday) you and your partner are available for testing. 
[/list]
Note that, depending on the test, you will spend between 30 minutes and two hours on testing.
After you submit your email we’ll get back to you with more information. You and your partner don’t both need to submit an email, one between you is enough!

Please note that there are certain requirements that will be used to determine who will be selected for puzzle testing.
Requirements:
[*]You have to be able to play the game in at least one of the weeks within the given timeframe.
[*]You have played We Were Here (Too) for at least an hour.
[*]Your Steam profile level is at least level 4.
[*]Your Steam profile is visible to us, so we can check these requirements.
[*]You have to be able to record both video and the audio of your playing session, and send them to us.
[*]You are able to give written feedback to us about your experience playing an early puzzle.
[*] You can communicate with us via our [url=https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?url=https://discord.gg/CPaReE3]Discord[/url].
[/list]
You will also be asked to agree to the following NDA:

[b]Non-Disclosure Agreement[/b]
In taking part in this early testing, you agree not to share information, screenshots, or video relating to the puzzles you experience. It goes without saying that the magic of the game is figuring out the puzzles with a friend, so we need to control what information is released before the game comes out. We hope you understand and appreciate your cooperation!

Our current testers have been exceptional with their comments and suggestions, and we’re hugely grateful. If you’d like to join them, we look forward to hearing from you!
